scope: Read-only FCR bid ranking, indivisibility, aggregate portfolio bids and low-price implications; no model changes

official_sources.institution: ANRE / Romanian Ministry of Justice legislative portal
official_sources.title: Regulament din 8 decembrie 2021 privind clauzele si conditiile pentru furnizorii de servicii de echilibrare si pentru furnizorii de rezerva de stabilizare a frecventei
official_sources.version: Retrieved portal version 2024-06-01, reflecting Order 18/2024; not represented as proof of every subsequent amendment
verified_facts: FCR offers are aggregated across a provider's UFR/GFR portfolio.
Offers exceeding the provider's total qualified capacity are rejected.
Valid offers are sorted ascending by price, with equal prices sorted chronologically.
The final offer completing required FCR capacity can only be fully accepted; total procurement may exceed the minimum requirement.
Each accepted offer is paid its own accepted bid price.

verified_facts: At most 10 quantity-price pairs per delivery interval, aggregated across qualified UFR/GFR.
Offered quantity must not exceed the published requirement.
Capacity is quoted per direction with equal up/down reserve, and prices in lei/hMW.
Ranking and pay-as-bid provisions agree with amended Articles 213-214.

interpretations: A valid 100 MW aggregate bid need not be prohibited solely because total requirement is 128 MW. Qualification, actual published tender quantity and deliverability remain prerequisites.
Lower compliant bid prices improve rank but also reduce the capacity remuneration received; low-price priority and historical system-average payment cannot be assumed simultaneously.
Indivisibility of an individual bid does not mean all bids of a 100 MW portfolio must win together. Several quantity-price pairs may produce a partially awarded portfolio.

If cheaper accepted bids have already fully met requirement, later bids are not accepted. If a positive gap remains, the marginal indivisible bid is accepted whole rather than automatically rejected for exceeding the remaining gap.
The existing 40 MW / 31.25 percent project cap is a research assumption, not an official supplier-share limit.
illustrative_assumptions: Demand 128 MW, cheaper bids 50 MW, valid marginal offer 100 MW: the whole offer fills the gap and aggregate procurement becomes 150 MW under the stated rule.

Bid price equivalent to EUR 1/MW/h and awarded capacity 100 MW: capacity cash EUR 100/h, before costs and performance adjustments. This is an illustrative converted price, not a verified market quote or price-bound claim.
